newsitem.title: USA: Condor released in Arizona found dead.
newsitem.headline: Condor released in Arizona found dead.

text.p: A seven-month-old male California candor, one of six recently released in northern Arizona, was apparently attacked and killed by a golden eagle, officials said on Monday.
The condor, which was hatched at the Los Angeles Zoo in May, may have been vulnerable to an attack because it never demonstrated the social skills typical of wild condors.

The condor, known as No. 42, roosted alone and at one point took a six-day, lone sortie miles from the flock and had to be captured by field crews and returned to Vermilion Cliffs, where the birds were released in December.

But the remaining five condors appear to be healthy and have developed a tight social unit, making them less vulnerable to predation, according to a joint statement released by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, the Arizona Game and Fish Department, The Bureau of Land Management and the Peregrine Fund.
